On Fri, Mar 1, 2019 at 1:13 AM Wilson Guillory <wilsonx...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I am working on a project that requires some automated tree manipulation. I need to write a function that creates two new trees given a BEAST tree with node error bars (95% confidence intervals for divergence time estimates). The two new trees are supposed to have node heights (and corresponding branch lengths) equal to the upper and lower 95CI values of the given tree. So for example, if the given tree has a node at 5±2 Ma, I need to make a tree with the node at 7 Ma and a tree with the node at 3 Ma. All nodes/branches in the tree must be adjusted in this way. The tree is ultrametric so branch lengths must also be adjusted to keep all tips at 0 Ma.
>
> Since this suite of R packages (ggtree, treeio, and tidytree) is the only ones I can find that can utilize BEAST node bar outputs, I'm trying to write the function in here. I'm close, but having some trouble. Here's my code so far:
>
> > # convert the starting tree to a "tibble"
> > LCItreetib <- as_tibble(starting_tree)
> > r <- nrow(LCItreetib)
> > # for every row in the tibble, copy the lower CI value for height, length, and rate
> > # into the true value slot. this makes the lower CI tree.
> > for (x in 1:r){
> >   LCItreetib$height[x] <- LCItreetib$height_0.95_HPD[[x]][2]
> >   LCItreetib$length[x] <- LCItreetib$length_0.95_HPD[[x]][2]
> >   LCItreetib$rate[x]   <- LCItreetib$rate_0.95_HPD[[x]][2]
> > }
> > LCItree <- as.treedata(LCItreetib)
>
> Basically I convert the tree into tibble format using tidytree. Then I grab the (in this case) lower estimate of the 95% confidence interval for all node heights, branch lengths, and rates, and replace the starting values with them. This makes a tibble where the actual node heights, branch lengths, and rates now correspond to the lower 95CI estimates of the starting tree. The 95CIs themselves remain unchanged but are not necessary for later analyses.
>
> When I convert the tibble back to a treedata object in the last line is where the trouble begins. I was initially optimistic when I plotted the tree with node height labels like this:
> >
> > ggtree(LCItree) + geom_text2(aes(subset=!isTip, label=round(height, digits=2)), nudge_y=0.12, nudge_x = -0.65) + theme_tree2()
>
> But I realized that, while the displayed node height labels are the values that I want, the actual shape of the tree has remained unchanged, as plotting the tree with the timescale (theme_tree2()) shows. When I compare the LCI tree to the starting tree, the trees are identical, the only difference being the node height labels themselves. It seems to me that the data that actually changes the tree's displayed shape is stored some other way but I do not know it.
>
> Thanks for any help you can provide,
> Wilson
>

> --
> 1. G Yu*, TTY Lam, H Zhu, Y Guan*. Two methods for mapping and visualizing associated data on phylogeny using ggtree. Molecular Biology and Evolution, 2018, 35(2):3041-3043. doi: 10.1093/molbev/msy194
